\chapter{Index Tricks: Cyclic Sort, Marking \& Permutation Cycles}
\label{ch:index_tricks}

\begin{tcolorbox}[enhanced, colback=white, colframe=secondaryblue, boxrule=1pt, arc=2mm]
\textbf{\large\textcolor{primaryblue}{When the values are $1..n$, a value is also an index: place every value home, mark by sign, and walk permutation cycles.}}
\end{tcolorbox}

\chapterfacts{1200}{2000}{5}{10}{30}

\begin{plannedbox}[Planned Contents --- this chapter is not written yet]
\textbf{Part A --- Lessons}
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*, label=\textbf{A\arabic*.}, itemsep=1pt]
    \item Values in $[1, n]$: the array as a function $i \mapsto a_i$
    \item Cyclic sort: put every value at its home index in $\bigO{n}$ swaps
    \item Marking in place: negation, adding $n$, and restoring the array
    \item Permutation cycles: decomposition, minimum swaps to sort, applying a permutation in place
    \item Missing and duplicate numbers: sums, XOR and index tricks compared
\end{enumerate}
